items.title: FAA grounds all US flights over communications outage
items.feedTitle: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, citing 'extraordinary circumstances' and 'reasons of safety' after a telecommunications outage disrupted air traffic control communications. The outage grounded thousands of flights and stranded millions of passengers. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a 'nefarious attack,' attributing the problem to a telecommunications failure. The FAA lifted the ground stop later Friday evening after identifying and addressing the issue.

items.title: SpaceX Starship reaches orbit despite booster catch failure
items.feedTitle: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
items.summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket successfully reached orbit on its 15th test flight Friday, though the company aborted its attempted double-catch of the booster when it malfunctioned and splashed into the ocean. Despite the setback, the spacecraft soared into orbit in what SpaceX called its boldest test yet, demonstrating progress toward full rocket reusability. The booster malfunction did not prevent the overall mission from advancing toward the company's goals.

items.title: Trump cabinet members feud over Nvidia scandal response
items.feedTitle: Trump’s top economic advisers clash over Lutnick’s handling of Nvidia
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia's most advanced chips, marking a visible rift among Trump's top economic advisers. The clash emerged from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO following allegations he had an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. Bessent's finger-pointing suggests internal disagreements over how the administration handled the national security breach.

items.title: ICE reports record deportations and arrests for fiscal year
items.feedTitle: ICE touts record number of deportations in agency's history
items.summary: The Department of Homeland Security announced that Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested more than 491,000 people and deported over 483,000 in the last fiscal year, marking all-time highs for the agency. The Trump administration has stated it aims to deport one million immigrants annually. The figures underscore the administration's immigration enforcement priorities and the scale of deportation operations.

items.title: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeats Rep. Lauren Boebert
items.feedTitle: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado loses U.S. House seat to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
items.summary: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert for a Colorado U.S. House seat Friday, ousting the three-term representative who had become a staple of conservative media. The race was called after election day, underscoring a Republican setback in what was thought to be a competitive GOP district. The victory marks a loss for Trump-backed candidates in the midterm results.

stlouis.title: Ameren plans three more Missouri battery plants
stlouis.feedTitle: Ameren plans three more Missouri battery plants
stlouis.summary: Ameren, a major energy utility, announced plans to develop three additional battery storage facilities in Missouri. The expansion reflects the company's investment in energy storage infrastructure to support grid reliability and renewable energy integration. Details about the locations and timeline for these projects were provided by the utility.

stlouis.title: Missouri hemp businesses shutter as restrictions take effect
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri hemp businesses clear shelves, close shops as new restrictions take effect
stlouis.summary: Hemp businesses across Missouri have been forced to clear shelves and close shops as new state restrictions took effect. The regulatory changes have disrupted the hemp industry, which has faced evolving legal frameworks governing sales and product types. Business operators have had to adjust their operations in response to the tighter compliance requirements.

stlouis.title: St. Louis expands shelter capacity for winter cold
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis expands shelter for cold weather
stlouis.summary: St. Louis announced an expansion of its emergency shelter services as winter weather approaches. The expansion is intended to provide additional capacity for homeless individuals during the colder months. The city's effort reflects planning for seasonal demand for shelter services.

items.title: Iran strikes US military radar in Bahrain in retaliation
items.feedTitle: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it targeted and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a U.S. airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik. The U.S. military said it downed two Iranian attack drones during the incident. The exchange marks an escalation of direct military confrontation between Iran and U.S. forces in the region, though the U.S. denies Iran's claim of successfully hitting the radar.

items.title: Microsoft outage disrupts services globally for 24 hours
items.feedTitle: Microsoft outage: company scrambles to fix global issue that took down Outlook and Teams
items.summary: A major Microsoft outage left Outlook, Teams, and Copilot offline worldwide for nearly 24 hours, affecting governments, businesses, hospitals, and schools globally. Microsoft apologized for the disruption and blamed a technical issue. Experts called the event a 'stark reminder' of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big technology providers. The outage highlighted systemic vulnerabilities in global digital infrastructure.

items.title: Trump plans first trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi
items.feedTitle: Trump to have first trilateral meeting with Putin, Xi
items.summary: President Trump plans to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China next week, marking the first-ever trilateral meeting between the three leaders. The unprecedented summit comes as Trump administration focuses on engagement with major powers. The meeting will cover issues ranging from nuclear non-proliferation to broader geopolitical concerns.

items.title: All passengers rescued in New Orleans cruise ship collision
items.feedTitle: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
items.summary: A tanker ship collided with a docked river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers on the Mississippi River in New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the vessel. All passengers and crew were accounted for with none critically injured in what the city's mayor called a 'miracle on the Mississippi.' Thirty-two people were taken to hospital with non-critical injuries. Rescue operations successfully evacuated everyone from the vessel.

items.title: Bus-truck collision kills 24 in Assam's Kaziranga
items.feedTitle: Students among 24 dead in bus-truck collision in Assam’s Kaziranga
items.summary: A collision between a truck and bus near Kaziranga in Assam killed at least 23-24 people, with several students among the deceased. The crash occurred on a major highway and prompted response from local authorities. The incident represents a significant transportation disaster in India's Assam state.

items.title: Microsoft outage hits Indian businesses and airline support
items.feedTitle: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
items.summary: The global Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook and cloud-based email services, affecting business operations and airline customer support services across India. Indian companies and public services reported disruption from the outage. Air India issued travel advisories in response to the communication disruption.

items.title: US assures India of tariff advantage over competitors
items.feedTitle: In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors
items.summary: The United States gave India assurances of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors in a major breakthrough for bilateral trade negotiations. India and the US aim to wrap up the first phase of a trade deal by next month's G20 Summit. The commitment signals preferential treatment for Indian exports in U.S. markets.

items.title: India's protest movement faces government crackdown post-summer
items.feedTitle: CJP: India’s protesters face government crackdown after summer victory
items.summary: India's youth protest movement, which gained momentum during summer with Gen Z-led dissent fueled by frustration and online satire, now faces government pressure and uncertainty heading into winter. The movement, which achieved initial victories around education and job concerns, confronts restrictions and harassment. The shift from summer mobilization to winter facing institutional resistance marks a critical juncture for the protest narrative.

items.title: Zakir Naik's Islamic foundation banned third time in India
items.feedTitle: Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation banned a third time in India, ‘terror-preacher’ still on the run
items.summary: India's government extended a ban on Islamic preacher Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) for a third time, through 2031, citing 'sinister anti-India designs.' Naik, who remains fugitive from Indian authorities, has been controversial for his firebrand messaging. The extended ban reflects government efforts to restrict the organization's activities and influence in India.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending deference to prior H-1B approvals
immigration.feedTitle: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security proposed removing a rule (8 CFR 214.1(c)(5)) that provides deference to prior USCIS approvals when adjudicating H-1B extension requests. Under the proposed rule—not yet final, with comments due November 13—workers seeking to renew their visas would face full re-evaluation rather than automatic approval based on previous approvals. The change could affect approximately 208,000 H-1B renewal cases annually and trigger up to 6,000 additional requests for evidence (RFEs).

immigration.title: State Department revokes 6,000+ visas for birth tourism
immigration.feedTitle: Protecting the Sanctity of U.S. Citizenship: A New Visa Restriction Policy for Those Who Engage in or Facilitate Birth Tourism
immigration.summary: The U.S. State Department announced a new visa restriction policy targeting over 6,000 foreigners involved in or facilitating 'birth tourism'—the practice of entering the U.S. to give birth to obtain citizenship for the child. The policy is finalized and in effect. It marks a significant enforcement action against the practice and reflects administration priorities on citizenship and immigration control.

immigration.title: DHS ends automatic EAD extensions for pending renewals
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security published an interim final rule (finalized and in effect as of October 30, 2025) ending automatic extensions of Employment Authorization Documents (Forms I-766 or EADs) for aliens who have timely filed applications to renew their EAD. Previously, applicants could work while their renewals were pending; under the new rule, authorization may lapse if processing delays occur. The change affects workers in various employment-based visa categories.

items.title: Trump advisers clash over Lutnick's Nvidia handling
items.feedTitle: Trump’s top economic advisers clash over Lutnick’s handling of Nvidia
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for failing to prevent export of Nvidia's advanced chips to China, escalating tensions within Trump's economic team. The conflict centers on the national security implications of Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. Bessent's accusations suggest internal disagreement over responsibility for the breach and point to possible discussions of Lutnick's ouster.

items.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end week lower amid Nvidia turmoil
items.feedTitle: US Stock Market Weekly Wrap: S&P 500 Gains 2.5% Despite Nvidia and AI Stock Selloff
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished lower Friday as Nvidia's leadership crisis weighed on technology stocks, though both indexes notched their best week since August. The AMD semiconductor sector sold off amid broader AI-chip uncertainty. Despite Friday's losses, the indexes managed weekly gains, with strength earlier in the week offsetting end-of-week weakness from the Nvidia scandal.

items.title: US wholesale prices rise to nearly four-year high in October
items.feedTitle: US producer prices rise moderately in October, but inflation broadens out
items.summary: U.S. wholesale inflation (producer prices) rose in October to the highest annual rate in nearly four years, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Prices rose 0.3% in October with an annual rate of 6.5%. The inflation broadening comes after earlier reports showed cooling consumer-level price pressures, suggesting stagflationary risks for the economy and pressures on Federal Reserve policy.

items.title: Home sales hit 16-year low as mortgage rates stay elevated
items.feedTitle: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid soaring mortgage rates
items.summary: Sales of existing homes in the U.S. fell to their lowest level in more than 16 years, dropping to 3.75 million units in October—an 8.8% decline from the prior year. Buyers have been driven away by elevated mortgage rates, now near three-year highs, and persistent inflation. The real estate market downturn reflects affordability pressures and consumer reluctance amid the challenging interest rate environment.

finance.note: Oil prices have eased as global supply returned to surplus for the first time since the start of the Iran conflict, with the IEA reporting oversupply of nearly 2 million barrels per day in October. U.S. stocks ended mixed Friday—the Dow up 0.1%, S&P 500 and Nasdaq down—but both major indexes recorded their best week since August despite Nvidia's scandal weighing on tech. Wholesale inflation pressures and elevated mortgage rates remain headwinds; watch Nvidia's earnings report and the Anthropic IPO for signals on AI sector momentum and valuation resilience.

cards.title: Friction is your friend
cards.insight: Making a desired behavior harder—not easier—often works better than removing obstacles. When people must pause and consciously choose each time (rather than follow an automatic path), awareness increases and impulsive choices drop. The Microsoft outage forced millions to slow down and reconsider their dependency on email.
cards.takeaway: For habits you want to break, add a deliberate friction point: put your phone in another room, require a written reason before checking email, or schedule a 5-minute delay before any purchase.

cards.title: Crisis reveals priority, not intention
cards.insight: During the FAA ground stop, millions claimed they 'needed' to travel; when truly blocked, most adapted within hours. This gap between stated and revealed preference suggests many habits persist not from necessity but from convenience. What we say we'll do under crisis and what we actually do are often very different.
cards.takeaway: Test your real priorities by temporarily removing the option for one week. If you adjust painlessly, it wasn't the priority you thought—and you've learned something true about yourself.

cards.title: Deference creates drift
cards.insight: The DHS proposal to end H-1B deference to prior approvals reflects a principle that habit: when a system automatically renews the old choice, scrutiny fades and drift occurs unnoticed. The same applies to personal habits—auto-renewals of subscriptions, recurring calendar blocks, and 'always done it this way' routines lock behavior in place without fresh decision-making.
cards.takeaway: Quarterly, audit your automatic commitments (subscriptions, recurring meetings, standing routines). Force yourself to re-approve each one from scratch, not as renewal but as a new choice.

cards.title: Transparency beats willpower
cards.insight: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet strategy—hiding the card details from the AI agent to prevent misuse—recognizes that willpower is fragile. Rather than trust the agent to behave, the system makes misbehavior structurally impossible. Habit change works the same way: design your environment so the wrong choice is harder than the right one.
cards.takeaway: Stop relying on self-discipline. Instead, engineer your context: delete apps, unsubscribe from tempting emails, pay bills automatically to a separate account, or ask a friend to hold you accountable in writing.

ai.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips found in China's AI models
ai.feedTitle: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
ai.summary: Research shows that China's most powerful AI models were trained on Nvidia's banned Blackwell chips, despite U.S. export controls designed to restrict access. The finding suggests illicit procurement networks or enforcement gaps in export restrictions. The revelation adds to scrutiny of the Nvidia scandal and raises questions about the effectiveness of U.S. technology export policy toward China.

ai.title: Fed cites AI as top financial system risk in latest survey
ai.feedTitle: HUD OCIO Plans Data and Artificial Intelligence Division
ai.summary: In its latest survey, the Federal Reserve identified artificial intelligence risks as the biggest threat to financial system stability, surpassing previous concerns about asset bubbles and leverage. The Fed is monitoring the rapid data center build-out for risks to the financial system. Central bankers are grappling with how AI valuations, computing power concentration, and unknown failure modes could destabilize markets.

ai.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, faster AI model
ai.feedTitle: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its new AI model built for speed
ai.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new generative AI model designed for speed and efficiency. The model powers Google's AI Mode in Search, which aims to provide better answers to complex queries and deliver richer visual responses. The launch reflects Google's push to advance its AI capabilities as competition intensifies in the generative AI space.

ai.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI shopping agents
ai.feedTitle: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
ai.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a feature that lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf without accessing actual card details. The rollout began with a limited test to U.S. Pro subscribers. The wallet aims to provide a safer way for AI agents to conduct transactions by creating a virtual payment interface that shields sensitive financial information.

ai.title: Jensen Huang's exit impacts AI startup funding outlook
ai.feedTitle: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
ai.summary: Venture capitalists and AI founders say Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO could significantly impact startup funding, as Nvidia has poured tens of billions into AI startups under his leadership. The concern is that Huang's successor may be less aggressive in supporting new ventures, potentially leading to smaller checks and lower valuations for AI startups. The transition raises questions about Nvidia's continued role in seeding the AI ecosystem.
